title: optimize-evals 1:1 prep - prompt set regressions + AB results
content:
Goal for 1:1 with Lena (2026-03-06)

Quick summary of what I want to cover:
- Surface major quality regressions detected in the last weekly run (2026-03-04)
- Walk through A/B results for prompt-set v3 vs v2 on customer-like traffic
- Decide on canary rollback vs fix+retry for two high-impact prompts
- Align on next steps for prompt curation + evaluation cadence

Context / TL;DR:
- Weekly evals found 3 regressions flagged by quality monitors: two are prompt-driven (P-142, P-149) and one appears model-variant drift (M-21).
- A/B test (v2 baseline vs v3 candidate) ran for 72h on ~120k requests; v3 improved avg logits for slot-filling by +6% but increased hallucination score on free-form queries (F1 drop ~4%).
- Customer-facing regression observed in sample CUSTOMER-ACCT-9 (incorrect legal term usage) mapped to prompt P-149.

Data / notes to reference during convo:
- Regression alerts:
  * P-142: precision drop on named-entity extraction across low-context prompts (detected by eval set NER-2026-02)
  * P-149: hallucination increase on legal-phrasing queries (sampled from prod logs)
  * M-21: minor BLEU-like drift on translation style task (likely unrelated to prompts)
- A/B metrics snapshot (v2 vs v3):
  * Coverage: v3 +2.1%
  * Slot accuracy (critical): v3 +6.0% (p < 0.01)
  * Hallucination rate (auto-detector): v3 +3.9% (p ~ 0.04)
  * Human eval (10 randoms): v2 preferred 6/10 for legal queries, v3 preferred 8/10 for slot-filling
- Risk assessment:
  * P-149 regression impacts a small set of high-risk customers (legal templates). High severity for those accounts.
  * P-142 affects internal downstream extractor; moderate severity but broad surface area.

Proposed options (talked-through):
1) Immediate canary rollback of v3 for routes tagged "legal-templates" + targeted rapid fix for P-149 (change prompt guardrail + add negative exemplars).
   - Pros: minimizes customer impact quickly.
   - Cons: loses v3 slot-filling gains on non-legal traffic.
2) Keep v3 globally but deploy prompt-level override: if route==legal-template -> route to v2; else v3. Add monitor for false negatives.
   - Pros: preserves gains for most traffic, surgical.
   - Cons: complexity in routing and testing; requires QA signoff.
3) Roll-forward with model-level tweak (temperature/prior) and expanded eval sets, hold off on rollback until human review for high-risk samples complete.

Suggested immediate actions for the meeting (decisions I want to get):
- Approve prompt-level override for "legal-templates" (short-term) OR approve full rollback. (Need Lena decision)
- If override chosen, assign owner for rollout: Jamie to implement routing rule + QA window (target: 24h).
- For P-142, approve adding 250 extra NER examples to eval set and schedule a focused retrain/finetune test (owner: Ethan).
- Increase human-eval sampling for hallucinatory cases from 10 -> 50 for next A/B (owner: Lena).

Action items (post-meeting follow-ups):
- [Ethan] Draft prompt P-149 fix (guardrail + 5 negative examples) and open PR with test harness by 2026-03-08.
- [Jamie] Implement routing override for legal-templates and run 12h smoke tests; report 2026-03-07 EOD.
- [Lena] Kick off expanded human eval (50 samples) and update dashboard to show hallucination per-route by 2026-03-10.
- [Ethan] Add 250 NER samples to eval set and run weekly eval; report delta on 2026-03-13 sync.
- [ProductOps] (optional) Notify the two affected customers with a short heads-up if rollback occurs.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is routing-by-route feasible in Dedicated + Private customers? (deployment complexity + config surface).
- Should we add a lightweight pre-filter classifier to detect legal-template queries and route them before generation? (adds latency but maybe cheaper than route-level split)
- How do we formalize severity thresholds for automatic rollback vs alerting? Current thresholds are somewhat hand-tuned.

Quick notes to self for how to present data in the meeting:
- Start with 1-slide summary: incidence + customer impact (1 chart showing hallucination delta for legal queries).
- Show example failure CUSTOMER-ACCT-9 with model outputs (clear before/after).
- Show A/B table (slot accuracy vs hallucination) and call out p-values.
- Propose recommended immediate action (prompt override) and ask for decision.

Misc small todo / reminders:
- Update eval harness to persist the full prompt+model+seed for any flagged hallucination cases.
- Add a short doc on "prompt guardrails" patterns we can reuse.
- Revisit thresholding logic for auto-detector - current threshold was tuned in Jan 2026 and might be stale.

Notes from previous sync (2026-02-28):
- We agreed on adding more negative exemplars for P-149 (didn't happen yet)
- Jamie planned routing experiments but got pulled to on-call; need to reassign.

End of prep doc. Keep this informal; I'll trim before sharing with wider group.
